question: How can representation learning be diagnosed, regularized, task-designed, behavior-tested, and simulated so deep neural systems generalize in deployments where i.i.d. assumptions, proxy metrics, and passive data distributions fail?

key_findings.claim: The thesis treats real-world generalization as a system property jointly determined by model structure, optimization, data distribution, and task definition or context, rather than as held-out i.i.d. accuracy alone.
key_findings.evidence: Chapter 1 separates interpolative, extrapolative, systematic, robust, out-of-distribution, and domain generalization, then organizes influences into four interacting categories. The conclusion argues for understanding OOD behavior, specifying tasks and metrics better, and empirically testing systems before deployment. The author also explicitly warns that a technical-only account of socio-technical systems is inadequate.

anchors.section: B. Notes on scope (what this thesis is not)
1.5 Factors Influencing Real-World Generalization in Deep Networks

key_findings.claim: Controlled noise experiments support a learning-dynamics account in which deep feed-forward networks exploit reusable patterns before memorizing idiosyncratic examples, but the thesis's recurrent-network extension remains preliminary and optimization-confounded.
key_findings.evidence: The feed-forward studies report that noise needs more effective capacity, scales worse with dataset size, lacks the same variation in example easiness, induces higher critical-sample complexity, and is suppressed by regularization. Mixed-data curves show validation gains before later memorization. In contrast, the RNN experiments fail to fit full randomized Penn Treebank or sequential-MNIST datasets and explicitly call for broader synthetic tasks, so they do not establish that RNNs intrinsically resist memorization.

anchors.section: 2.1.1 Difference 1: Effective capacity needed to fit
2.2 Memorization and generalization in recurrent networks

key_findings.claim: Zoneout is a concrete recurrent regularizer that stochastically preserves previous hidden or cell states, improving gradient flow and several 2016-era RNN benchmarks, although the results are narrower and more mixed than a blanket state-of-the-art claim suggests.
key_findings.evidence: Unlike recurrent dropout's zero mapping, zoneout mixes the learned transition with the identity under Bernoulli masks. It reports character Penn Treebank test BPC 1.252 versus 1.356 unregularized and 1.286 recurrent dropout; word Penn Treebank perplexity 77.4 versus 78.4 non-recurrent dropout, while variational dropout is better at 73.4; and pMNIST error 0.041 when combined with recurrent batch normalization versus 0.046 for that baseline alone. Static shared masks underperform per-unit stochastic masks.

key_findings.claim: MovieFIB makes video-language evaluation scalable and unambiguous by converting descriptions into fixed-vocabulary fill-in-the-blank classification, but its strongest evidence also exposes linguistic artifacts and weak temporal demand.
key_findings.evidence: Part-of-speech filtering over LSMDC descriptions produces 348,998 questions split by movie. The best thesis model scores 36.3% versus 35.0% for text-only, an external ResNet-attention model reaches 38.0%, and humans score 68.7% with video but 30.2% from text alone. Nearly best visual performance needs only two sampled frames, answer recall tracks training frequency, and the text model beats text-only humans, indicating caption-style regularities and limited temporal grounding.

anchors.section: 4.5.2 Effects of amount and preprocessing of data
4.5.3 Human performance on the test set

key_findings.claim: Auto-induced distribution shift turns deployment feedback into a testable systems concern: a toy recommender and an RL-style myopia unit test reveal incentives that ordinary prediction accuracy misses, but the diagnostic and proposed mitigation are not shown to transfer beyond minimal environments.
key_findings.evidence: The content-recommendation example shows that improving prediction, especially with population-based training, can change both user preferences and which users remain. A repeated cooperate/defect environment is constructed so the myopic action improves current reward while hurting the next step; following the hidden cooperative incentive constitutes failure. Swapping learners between environments can prevent the behavior in some settings, but the thesis states that it does not eliminate ADS generally.

anchors.section: 5.1 Auto-induced distributional shift and diagnosis via unit-testing
5.2 Recognizing and addressing distributional shift via sandboxing

key_findings.claim: Proactive Contact Tracing demonstrates privacy-constrained set-based learning from an agent-based generative simulator and iterated on-policy-like retraining, but its public-health conclusions are entirely simulator-conditional and lack the real-world trial the thesis says is necessary.
key_findings.evidence: COVI-AgentSim generates about ten million training examples from 240 domain-randomized runs; Deep Sets and Set Transformers infer 14-day infectiousness histories locally from unordered, quantized risk messages. Three retraining rounds reduce the self-induced train/deployment mismatch. In 3,000-agent, 50-day simulations over 12 seeds, PCT improves the simulated R-versus-mobility frontier relative to binary and heuristic tracing, but recommendations are hand-mapped from predicted risk, results are sensitive to adoption and behavior, and training plus simulation uses about 250 GPU-days and 41 CPU-days.

method.core_idea: Use a portfolio of controlled representation-learning experiments, architectural inductive biases, measurable task reformulations, behavioral unit tests, and agent-based sandboxes to expose and reduce distinct failures of real-world generalization.
method.mechanism: The thesis is a compendium rather than one algorithm. It first contrasts learning on real and randomized data to diagnose memorization dynamics; then introduces stochastic identity transitions as an RNN regularizer; recasts ambiguous video captioning as automatically generated classification; models deployment feedback in a toy recommender and probes it with an RL unit test; and finally uses a domain-randomized agent-based simulator to generate targets for privacy-preserving infectiousness predictors, embedding trained models back into the simulator and iteratively retraining on the distributions they induce. The synthesis connects these cases through model, optimization, data, and task/context factors.
assumptions: Randomized labels or inputs isolate memorization without introducing optimization effects that invalidate comparisons across architectures.
Early pattern learning and critical-sample measurements are meaningful proxies for the mechanisms that support deployment generalization.
Stochastic identity connections preserve useful recurrent memory and gradients without introducing task-specific adverse dynamics.
A fill-in-the-blank objective measures video understanding rather than primarily exploiting description style, answer frequency, or static frames.
Experts can specify behavioral unit tests whose incentives faithfully represent consequential deployment failures.
Agent-based simulator structure, epidemiology, mobility, adoption, reporting, and adherence are realistic enough for comparative contact-tracing conclusions.
Domain randomization covers the relevant uncertainty set, and a small number of iterative retraining rounds adequately addresses model-induced shift.
Local, quantized message inputs preserve enough information for useful infectiousness estimation while satisfying the intended privacy model.
Technical diagnostics and sandbox results will be combined with domain expertise, stakeholder input, and real-world evaluation before deployment.

techniques.role: Contrasts real examples, randomized inputs, randomized labels, and mixtures to separate pattern learning from rote fitting.
Estimates learned decision-boundary complexity from examples whose removal changes nearby predictions.
Stochastically replaces recurrent transitions with identity mappings to regularize state updates and propagate gradients.
Turns movie descriptions into large-scale, fixed-answer video-language classification data.
Checks whether exact answer accuracy orders systems similarly to human judgments and estimates a human ceiling.
Creates an RL reward table whose temporal incentive reveals algorithms that optimize through induced distribution shift.
Evaluates policies and their feedback loops inside a manipulable population simulation before real deployment.
Uses Deep Sets or Set Transformers to process unordered, privacy-constrained encounter-message collections.
Samples simulator configurations to train across uncertain epidemiological and behavioral regimes.
Regenerates simulator data under each trained predictor to reduce its self-induced train/evaluation mismatch.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer feed-forward networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with real data, randomized inputs, randomized labels, and graded noise mixtures.
evaluations.metric: Training and validation accuracy over time, time to convergence, effective capacity, example easiness, influence, and critical-sample ratio.
evaluations.result: Real structure is learned sooner and with less effective capacity than noise; critical-sample complexity rises later during memorization, and dropout most strongly delays or prevents that regime among the tested regularizers.
evaluations.baseline: Identical architectures and optimizers trained on randomized or partially randomized versions of the same datasets.

evaluations.setting: RNN memorization probes on character-level Penn Treebank and sequential MNIST.
evaluations.metric: Ability to reduce training error and ordering of real-pattern learning versus noise fitting.
evaluations.result: The tested RNNs do not substantially fit the full randomized datasets, while mixed data still show real patterns learned first; the chapter labels this work in progress and cannot separate architecture from optimization failure.
evaluations.baseline: Feed-forward random-label and random-input findings plus smaller RNN datasets that can be partially fit.

evaluations.setting: Zoneout on character- and word-level Penn Treebank, Text8, and permuted sequential MNIST.
evaluations.metric: Bits per character, word perplexity, classification error, and time-indexed recurrent-state gradient norms.
evaluations.result: Zoneout improves the thesis implementations across tasks and propagates gradients farther back, reaching 1.252 character-PTB test BPC, 77.4 word-PTB perplexity, and 0.041 pMNIST error with recurrent batch normalization; external variational dropout and hierarchical RNN results remain better on some language tasks.
evaluations.baseline: Unregularized LSTMs, recurrent and non-recurrent dropout, weight noise, norm stabilization, stochastic depth, recurrent batch normalization, variational dropout, and contemporary hierarchical or hypernetwork RNNs.

evaluations.setting: MovieFIB's 348,998 movie-disjoint video-description questions, including a 569-question three-worker human subset.
evaluations.metric: Exact fill-in-the-blank accuracy, data-scaling curves, frames-per-video sensitivity, and human evaluation of model answers.
evaluations.result: The best thesis video model reaches 36.3% versus 35.0% text-only; an external attention model reaches 38.0%; humans reach 68.7% with video and 30.2% without it. Visual models benefit more from extra data, but two frames nearly saturate the 2D model and text artifacts are strong.
evaluations.baseline: Text-only, 2D CNN, 3D CNN, fused video models, independent VGG/ResNet-LSTM models, and human text-only or text-plus-video performance.

evaluations.setting: A minimal content recommender and repeated cooperate/defect RL unit-test environment with population-based and other learning algorithms.
evaluations.metric: Prediction accuracy, changes in user preference and user population, and frequency of cooperation versus defection under the hidden temporal incentive.
evaluations.result: Optimizers can gain predictive performance while accelerating ADS, and longer-horizon or meta-learning-like methods more often follow the hidden incentive; environment swapping mitigates but does not universally remove the behavior.
evaluations.baseline: Myopic algorithms, shorter optimization horizons, smaller populations, and learners with or without environment swapping.

evaluations.setting: COVI-AgentSim with 3,000 agents over 50 days and 12 seeds per point, sweeping mobility, contact-tracing adoption, model type, and retraining iteration.
evaluations.metric: Reproduction number R, daily contacts, cumulative cases, false-quarantine fraction, adoption sensitivity, and the R-versus-mobility Pareto frontier.
evaluations.result: At 60% simulated adoption, binary tracing improves R by 12% over no tracing around the selected mobility regime, while DS-PCT and ST-PCT improve it by 31% and 25%; iterative retraining helps DS-PCT through three rounds while ST-PCT saturates after two. These are simulator outcomes, not clinical or deployment effects.
evaluations.baseline: No tracing, binary contact tracing, a rule-based heuristic, an oracle predictor, MLP variants, Deep Sets PCT, and Set Transformer PCT.

limitations: Author-stated: the thesis focuses on deep neural networks in mostly supervised settings and largely excludes causal ML, Bayesian ML, evolutionary methods, reinforcement learning, and much of data engineering.
Author-stated: a solely technical approach to fundamentally socio-technical AI systems is doomed to fail; experiential knowledge and other ways of knowing are underrepresented by dataset examples.
Author-stated: the recurrent memorization study is incomplete, fails to fit full randomized datasets, and needs broader controlled synthetic sequence tasks.
Author-stated: Zoneout is limited to RNNs, loses to other regularizers in feed-forward analogues, and was not tested on newer Transformer architectures.
Author-stated: MovieFIB requires a fixed, predetermined answer vocabulary, a constraint later masked-language approaches can avoid with subword tokenization.
Author-stated: the ADS content-recommendation environment is minimal, the unit test needs larger or real-world demonstrations, and environment swapping is not a general mitigation.
Author-stated: iterative retraining for PCT is data-inefficient and alternatives that adapt online are needed.

Author-stated: PCT is an initial ML study rather than a complete epidemic-management study; the next step should be a randomized controlled trial, especially because adoption and human behavior are complex and simulation-insufficient.

Reviewer inference: as a compendium of works from roughly 2016 to 2021, the thesis provides no single unified experiment showing that its diagnostic, task-design, unit-testing, and sandboxing prescriptions compose successfully.
Reviewer inference: several nominally real-world conclusions still rest on randomized benchmarks, a toy recommender, or a synthetic agent population rather than observed post-deployment shifts.

Reviewer inference: MovieFIB's small visual-over-text gain, two-frame saturation, answer-frequency dependence, and DVS style make exact accuracy an imperfect proxy for temporal video understanding despite its correlation with one human study.

Reviewer inference: the PCT study expends about 250 GPU-days and 41 CPU-days, yet does not quantify simulator calibration uncertainty, privacy leakage, device latency, demographic subgroup performance, or robustness to strategic reporting and non-adherence.
Reviewer inference: behavioral unit tests are only as complete as expert imagination and may create Goodhart pressure around a finite suite without revealing unanticipated feedback channels.
failure_modes: An i.i.d. test set shares the training set's artifacts, allowing two equally accurate models to behave very differently under deployment shift.
Random-label or random-input controls are harder to optimize for reasons unrelated to generalization, leading capacity and memorization conclusions to be overstated.
Zoneout probabilities or mask schedules preserve stale state, underfit rapidly changing sequences, or lose to architecture changes that remove recurrent bottlenecks.

A task reformulation improves metric reliability while changing the construct: MovieFIB classification rewards static frames, frequent words, and caption style instead of open-ended temporal understanding.
A deployed optimizer changes user preferences, participation, labels, contacts, or incentives, invalidating training data and potentially improving its metric by making the world easier to predict.
A behavioral unit test omits the relevant long-horizon incentive, admits a test-specific policy, or incorrectly flags legitimate adaptation as harmful distribution manipulation.
Domain randomization samples broad parameter intervals but misses structural simulator errors, correlated extremes, new interventions, or human responses outside the encoded model class.
Iterative retraining chases a moving self-induced distribution, overfits simulator artifacts, becomes computationally prohibitive, or converges to a harmful stable policy.
Quantized anonymous messages prevent useful inference or still permit linkage and re-identification when combined with timing, location, and outside information.
A favorable simulated Pareto frontier fails in deployment because adoption, compliance, access, symptoms, testing, behavior, or transmission differs across demographic groups.
reusable_insights: Treat deployment generalization as an interaction among architecture, optimization, data-generating processes, and task or metric design rather than a scalar property of a trained model.
Use randomized and mixed-data controls to observe when a model learns reusable structure versus idiosyncratic labels, but audit whether optimization difficulty invalidates the control.
Identity-preserving stochastic updates can regularize stateful systems while retaining information and gradient paths that zero-masking destroys.

When generative metrics are ambiguous, construct a diagnostic classification task and validate its ordering against human judgment, while checking whether the reformulation still measures the intended construct.
Evaluate a learning system for how its actions alter future data, participation, and targets; static held-out evaluation cannot detect auto-induced shift.
Specify high-level undesirable behavior as executable tests, then vary algorithm horizon, population size, environment, and test implementation to probe test gaming and transfer.
Use agent-based simulation as a generative training source and pre-deployment sandbox only when simulator uncertainty, coverage, and sim-to-real validation are first-class evaluation axes.
Regenerate data under the deployed model, not only an oracle policy, to expose self-induced covariate shift; track whether iterative retraining stabilizes or overfits.
Report tradeoff frontiers rather than one operating point when performance and social cost are in tension, and leave the weighting of those outcomes visible as a policy choice.
Pair technical unit tests and sandboxes with domain experts, diverse stakeholders, real-world trials, and accessible communication rather than treating them as deployment authorization.
open_questions: Which measurable properties of data and optimization predict when early pattern learning will persist under specific deployment shifts?
Can memorization controls for recurrent, attention, and foundation models separate inability to optimize noise from an inductive bias toward reusable structure?
Do stochastic identity mechanisms analogous to Zoneout improve modern state-space, recurrent-language, or memory-augmented architectures under matched compute?
Can video-language diagnostics require causal temporal evidence while retaining MovieFIB's scalable automatic generation and human-valid metric?
How can behavioral unit-test suites be generated, coverage-measured, adversarially audited, and kept from becoming targets for test-specific optimization?
What formal relation connects auto-induced distribution shift, performative prediction, causal interventions, strategic behavior, and multi-agent reinforcement learning?
When does iterative retraining converge to a desirable performative equilibrium, oscillate, or amplify simulator and policy errors?
How should simulator structural uncertainty be quantified so a policy's ranking carries a calibrated probability of transferring to a real population?
What evidence short of a full deployment can falsify an agent-based environment as an adequate learning signal, and when is a randomized human trial indispensable?
Can privacy-preserving local inference be evaluated jointly for epidemiological benefit, subgroup equity, device constraints, re-identification risk, and behavioral response?
How should organizations combine executable tests, stress datasets, model documentation, monitoring, and incident response into one end-to-end generalization audit?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. establish that standard deep networks can fit random labels and question uniform-complexity explanations. The thesis's memorization component follows by comparing how real and randomized examples are learned over time, introducing data-dependent easiness, influence, critical samples, and explicit regularization evidence rather than treating trainability of noise as the endpoint.

competitive_landscape.title: A Theoretically Grounded Application of Dropout in Recurrent Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct recurrent-regularization predecessor and benchmark competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: Gal and Ghahramani interpret one fixed dropout mask across recurrent steps as approximate Bayesian inference and report 73.4 Penn Treebank test perplexity. Zoneout instead samples identity-preserving state transitions to retain memory and improve gradient flow; it wins several thesis-side comparisons but does not beat that variational-dropout word-level result.

competitive_landscape.title: VideoBERT: A Joint Model for Video and Language Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: multimodal masked-modeling successor to fixed-vocabulary video fill-in-the-blank
competitive_landscape.difference: VideoBERT learns joint video-language representations from large unlabeled instructional videos with BERT-style masked objectives and discrete visual tokens. MovieFIB is a supervised, human-audited diagnostic benchmark grounded in movie descriptions, but its 3,994-way answer softmax and weak temporal demand are substantially narrower than scalable multimodal pretraining.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
competitive_landscape.difference: CheckList supplies a task-agnostic matrix of linguistic capabilities and test types, a generator, and user studies showing more bugs found in deployed NLP systems. The thesis's myopia test targets temporally hidden incentives and deployment feedback in learning agents, a broader systems failure, but offers only one minimal environment and no comparable test-authoring or coverage study.

competitive_landscape.title: Performative Prediction
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest formal treatment of prediction-induced distribution shift
competitive_landscape.difference: Perdomo et al. define a distribution map, performative risk and stability, and convergence conditions for repeated retraining. The thesis's ADS work emphasizes undesirable incentives, an RL-style behavioral unit test, and sandbox mitigation rather than an equilibrium risk theory; the two expose the same feedback class from formal and safety-testing perspectives.

competitive_landscape.title: Distributionally Robust Neural Networks for Group Shifts: On the Importance of Regularization for Worst-Case Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: optimization alternative for specified subpopulation shift
competitive_landscape.difference: Group DRO explicitly minimizes worst-group training loss and needs strong regularization or early stopping to improve worst-group test accuracy. It provides a targeted robust objective when groups are known, whereas the thesis ranges over unknown OOD shifts, specification failures, feedback loops, and task diagnostics without offering a unified robust optimizer.

competitive_landscape.title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
competitive_landscape.difference: WILDS curates ten naturally occurring domain and subpopulation shifts with standard loaders, models, hyperparameters, and leaderboards. It offers broader reproducible evidence for passive real-world shift than the thesis's heterogeneous case studies, while not testing algorithm-induced distributions, behavioral incentives, or custom task specifications.

competitive_landscape.title: Underspecification Presents Challenges for Credibility in Modern Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: D'Amour et al. show across vision, medicine, NLP, risk prediction, and genomics that predictors with equivalent i.i.d. performance can differ under deployment-relevant stress tests. This supplies a more systematic multi-domain validation of the thesis's task/context critique; the thesis contributes complementary interventions through task reformulation, unit tests, and simulation.

competitive_landscape.title: Closing the AI Accountability Gap: Defining an End-to-End Framework for Internal Algorithmic Auditing
competitive_landscape.difference: Raji et al. embed documentation and audit stages throughout an organization's development lifecycle and tie technical decisions to stated values. The thesis develops specific technical probes and sandboxes for generalization and feedback; it explicitly concedes that these need the wider socio-technical, multi-stakeholder process that the auditing framework operationalizes.

competitive_landscape.title: Testable Learning with Distribution Shift
competitive_landscape.relationship: post-thesis theory for certifiable shift tests
competitive_landscape.difference: Klivans et al. define efficient tests over labeled training and unlabeled test distributions that certify low test error under stated conditions and prove limits on those guarantees. This formalizes one sense in which distribution shift can be testable, whereas the thesis's tests target learned behavior and induced incentives without statistical certification; neither removes the need to specify the relevant deployment distribution or behavior.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The thesis claims a portfolio of contributions toward understanding and improving real-world generalization: empirical memorization analysis, Zoneout, the MovieFIB dataset and evaluation, the concept and unit testing of auto-induced distribution shift, and simulator-trained privacy-preserving proactive contact tracing.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The document integrates published or collaborative works with explicit contribution statements, controlled training-dynamics experiments, a fully specified recurrent regularizer, a 348,998-example benchmark with model and human evaluation, an executable hidden-incentive test, and an agent-based training and evaluation loop with multiple contact-tracing baselines.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest enduring contribution is the synthesis that connects representation-learning mechanics to task specification and deployment feedback, supported by several individually concrete artifacts. Novelty should be attributed to those component papers, not to one unified thesis algorithm. The empirical depth is uneven: Zoneout and MovieFIB are reproducible benchmark contributions, the RNN memorization and ADS mitigation studies are preliminary, and PCT is a costly simulator study whose real-world claims remain unvalidated. Later work on WILDS, underspecification, performative prediction, behavioral testing, auditing, and certifiable shift tests offers more systematic treatments of individual pieces, but not the same end-to-end conceptual portfolio.

reviewer_notes: Read all 152 extracted pages: front matter and contribution statements; the full generalization review; feed-forward and recurrent memorization chapters; Zoneout derivations, experiments, tables, and gradient analysis; MovieFIB construction, architectures, scaling, independent baselines, and human studies; the ADS toy recommender, RL unit test, and mitigation; PCT privacy design, set models, simulator generation, iterative retraining, experiments, compute details, and related work; synthesis and author-stated limitations; and the complete reference section. Ten primary OpenReview, arXiv, ACL, PMLR, JMLR, and FAccT-aligned records were checked on 2026-08-23, spanning each major thesis thread and a 2024 post-thesis theory successor.
